specialty: Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology
source: ACGME Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology Milestones 2.0

level_1: Identifies patients who may benefit from advanced therapies
Manages patients peri- operatively and selects immunosuppressive therapy based on institutional protocol
Optimizes selection of patients to meet the fiduciary responsibility to the patient, the program, and the community
level_2: Evaluates patients using program selection criteria
Identifies complications of immunosuppression and comorbidities post- transplant
Manages the interdisciplinary team to formulate a care plan to achieve the best possible outcome
level_3: Participates in the evaluation of donors using program selection criteria and performs ongoing reassessment of the patient for continued eligibility for transplant
Determines whether to list a patient for transplant and selects optimal timing based on a complete evaluation
Integrates patient and program specific characteristics to estimate and optimize expected outcomes
level_4: Uses institutional protocol to care for patients post- transplant
Manages donor selection prior to transplant and manages early post-transplant complications (e.g., primary graft failure, rejection)
level_5: Formulates a plan based on hemodynamics, risk assessment, and comorbidities and benefits of continued medical therapy
Manages complications of immunosuppression and comorbidities post- transplant

level_1: Identifies patients at various stages of cardiogenic shock in need of temporary mechanical support
Manages patients on durable left ventricular assist device support devices
level_2: Recognizes the patient with chronic heart failure (Stage D) in need of a durable left ventricular assist device
Manages the intra- and early post-operative complications associated with temporary mechanical circulatory support devices
level_3: Demonstrates the ability to evaluate a patient for temporary mechanical support device
Manages complications of patients on durable mechanical circulatory devices including, but not limited to, bleeding, pump thrombosis, pump failure, and stroke
level_4: Demonstrates the ability to assess suitability of a patient for durable left ventricular assist device support based on current guidelines and institutional protocols
Optimizes patient care by negotiating the complex care of patients on temporary mechanical support devices during the weaning process and recognizes futility of further treatment
level_5: Manages patients on temporary mechanical support devices
Manages end-of-life care for patients on durable mechanical circulatory devices

level_1: Identifies patients with new onset heart failure based on signs, symptoms, and other given variables
Distinguishes various levels of shock based on clinical, lab, and diagnostic variables as described by clinical expert consensus
Evaluates barriers, including social determinants, that might lead to high risk of readmission
level_2: Recognizes acutely decompensated heart failure without shock (heart failure profiles)
Formulates plan based on diagnosis for optimizing guideline-directed medical therapy and device therapy
Recognizes time and indication for temporary support device and escalation of care
level_3: Recognizes acutely decompensated heart failure with shock
Optimizes inpatient management with diuretic protocols/algorithms and optimization of guideline- directed medical therapy to assure compensation and response to management before discharge
Discusses long-term prognosis and outcomes associated with guideline- directed medical therapy, including basic data and risk assessment models to increase patient understanding/awareness
level_4: Evaluates differential diagnosis and selects testing necessary for diagnosis according to guidelines
Manages each level of shock as indicated by guidelines/consensus and internal protocol
Plans for patient-specific transitions of care to maintain outpatient follow up and prevent readmissions using all available resources
level_5: Evaluates the etiology for readmission and works to improve cardiac, medical, or patient-related etiologies
Recognizes the significance of heart failure education for newly diagnosed heart failure and educates the patient on self-care, warning signs, and action plans
Uses multidisciplinary team for early patient assessment; integrates program-specific guidelines to initiate evaluation for advanced therapies

level_1: Recognizes clinical signs and symptoms of chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
Manages patients with stable chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

Effectively participates in team-based care, including palliative care, in management of advanced or end-stage chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
level_2: Recognizes clinical signs and symptoms of chronic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Manages patients with stable chronic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Manages an outpatient chronic heart failure program
level_3: Monitors patients for complications or changes related to chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
With indirect supervision, effectively participates in team-based care in management of common chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Advances quality of clinical practice in the treatment strategies for chronic heart failure
level_4: Monitors patients for complications or changes related to chronic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Manages patients with advanced and end- stage chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
Effectively develops and implements team-based care models in management of chronic heart failure
level_5: With direct supervision, effectively participates in team-based care in management of common chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Manages patients with advanced and end- stage chronic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

level_1: Discusses the clinical features of pulmonary hypertension
Develops team-based care and treatment strategies for pulmonary hypertension, with supervision
level_2: Discusses risk factors, outcomes, and survival of patients with pulmonary hypertension
Independently interprets testing results to develop individual treatment strategies for pulmonary hypertension
level_3: Identifies the basic evaluation of the patient with pulmonary hypertension, including history and physical, echocardiogram, hemodynamic evaluation, and laboratory evaluation
Independently develops individual treatment strategies for pulmonary hypertension, including lung or heart-lung transplant referral
level_4: Discusses options for therapy for pulmonary hypertension
Advances quality of clinical practice in the treatment strategies for pulmonary hypertension
level_5: Selects tests for the evaluation and monitoring of the patient with pulmonary hypertension
Identifies strategies to develop a pulmonary hypertension program

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of the indications for and contraindications to heart transplantation
Knows the strengths and limitations of strategies used to detect, monitor, and treat transplant rejection
level_2: Knows the principles of immunology pertinent to heart transplantation
Applies knowledge of potential complications after heart transplantation to optimize patient outcomes
level_3: Knows the intra- and early post-operative complications of heart transplantation
Applies knowledge of transplant immunology and pharmacology to optimize patient outcomes
level_4: Knows the mechanism of action, adverse effects, and drug-drug interactions of immunosuppressant therapies
Demonstrates knowledge of the pillars of a successful heart transplant program, including outcomes and resource allocation
level_5: Knows the long-term complications of heart transplantation

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of the characteristics of temporary mechanical support devices
Knows the clinical determinants favoring left ventricular assist device versus transplantation as long-term durable strategies
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of the characteristics of durable mechanical support devices
Applies knowledge of selection and use of temporary mechanical circulatory assist devices to optimize patient outcomes
level_3: Knows the indications for and contraindications for temporary mechanical circulatory support
Applies knowledge of selection and use of durable mechanical circulatory assist devices to optimize patient outcomes
level_4: Knows the indications for and contraindications for durable mechanical circulatory support
Demonstrates knowledge of the pillars of a successful mechanical circulatory support program, including outcomes and resource allocation
level_5: Knows intra- and early post-operative complications of temporary mechanical circulatory support

level_1: Lists a differential diagnosis for common clinical presentations for heart failure patients
Justifies optimal therapeutic option based on individual heart failure patient presentation
level_2: Lists therapeutic options for common clinical presentations for heart failure patients
Diagnoses patients with challenging heart failure presentations and uncommon disorders
level_3: Provides a comprehensive differential diagnosis for a wide range of clinical heart failure presentations
Develops therapeutic plan for patients with challenging heart failure presentations and uncommon disorders
level_4: Explains risks and benefits of standard therapeutic options for heart failure
Advances knowledge in pathophysiology and treatment of heart failure
level_5: Provides a focused differential diagnosis based on individual heart failure patient presentation
Disseminates knowledge of challenging heart failure presentations and uncommon disorders

level_1: Knows types of advanced heart failure diagnostics
Applies knowledge of appropriate selection and use of diagnostics for patients with complex advanced heart failure patients
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of indications and contraindications of advanced heart failure diagnostics
Identifies key diagnostic findings in complex advanced heart failure conditions
level_3: Knows the basic measurements and data output from the various advanced heart failure diagnostics
Advances knowledge in indications, contraindications, and appropriate use for advanced heart failure diagnostics
level_4: Demonstrates knowledge of appropriate selection and use of diagnostics for the routine advanced heart failure population
Advances knowledge in defining the role of advanced heart failure diagnostics
level_5: Identifies key diagnostic findings in common advanced heart failure conditions

level_1: Discusses the World
Discusses the pathophysiology of pulmonary hypertension
Integrates all options in the treatment of pulmonary hypertension including drugs, surgical procedures, and lung transplantation
level_2: Health Organization (WHO) classifications of pulmonary hypertension
Discusses the pharmacology of the drugs used in pulmonary hypertension
level_3: Discusses the types of drugs used to treat pulmonary hypertension
Assesses prognosis in pulmonary hypertension
level_4: Discusses physiology of the right ventricle and distinction between and pre- and post-capillary pulmonary hypertension
Identifies treatment modalities, including investigational agents and multi-drug regimens
level_5: Identifies drugs used to treat different classes of pulmonary hypertension
Demonstrates knowledge of the pillars of a multidisciplinary pulmonary hypertension program

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Describes quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or departmental level
Discloses patient safety events to patients and their families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and their families (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Participates in quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or departmental level
Role models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations, effectively using the roles of the interprofessional teams
Adapts practice to address barriers to adherence of care
level_2: Identifies key elements for effective transitions of care
Performs effective transitions of care in complex clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of improvements
level_3: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations, effectively using the roles of the interprofessional teams
Identifies barriers to adherence of care to specific populations
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes
level_4: Performs effective transitions of care in routine clinical situations
Role models effective coordination of patient- centered care among different disciplines and specialties
Leads innovations and advocates for populations with health care barriers
level_5: Demonstrates general knowledge of barriers to adherence to care
Role models and advocates for effective transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the health care system (e.g., hospital, skilled nursing facility, finance, personnel, technology)
Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
Applies knowledge in non-clinical topics needed for independent practice
level_2: Describes basic health payment systems, (e.g., government, private, public, uninsured care) and practice models
Engages with patients in shared decision making, informed by each patient’s payment models
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care and transition of care
level_3: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and how this impacts patient care
Seeks knowledge in non- clinical topics needed for independent practice (e.g., malpractice insurance, government regulation, compliance)
Participates in health policy advocacy activities
level_4: Delivers care with consideration of each patient’s payment model (e.g., insurance type)
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care and transition of care
Educates others in non- clinical topics to prepare them for independent practice
level_5: Demonstrates essential skills for documentation required for independent practice (e.g., electronic health record, documentation required for billing and coding)
Advocates for patient care needs (e.g., community resources, patient assistance resources) with consideration of the limitations of each patient’s payment model

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and use available evidence to manage a patient with cardiac disease
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences to guide evidence-based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence to the care of patients with complex cardiac disease while integrating patient preference
level_4: Critically appraises and applies available, potentially conflicting evidence to guide care of an individual patient
level_5: Develops initiatives to educate others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals
Creates and implements a learning plan
level_2: Acknowledges limits and gaps between expectations and performance; demonstrates self- awareness
Systematically seeks feedback and performance data with adaptability and humility
level_3: Demonstrates openness to feedback and performance data to form goals
Uses performance data to assess learning plan and improves it when necessary
level_4: Analyzes the factors which contribute to limits and gaps; demonstrates appropriate help-seeking behaviors
Coaches others to seek feedback and performance data
level_5: Occasionally seeks feedback and performance data with adaptability and humility
Facilitates the design and implementation of learning plans for others

level_1: Identifies and describes potential triggers for professionalism lapses
Recognizes the need to seek help in managing and resolving complex ethical situations
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of ethical principles (e.g., informed consent, advance directives, confidentiality, patient autonomy)
Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in oneself and others
level_3: Demonstrates insight into professional behavior in routine situations
Uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas (e.g., ethics consultations, risk management)
level_4: Applies knowledge of ethical principles to routine situations
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_5: Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks and responsibilities, identifies potential contributing factors, and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion in the future
Seeks assistance in managing personal relationships with industry and other entities to minimize bias and undue influence in practice
level_2: Recognizes the principles of conflict of interest in relationships with industry and other entities
Recognizes situations that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations
Identifies, discloses, and manages relationships with industry and other entities to minimize bias and undue influence in practice
level_4: Recognizes personal potential conflicts with industry
Engages with the system to improve outcomes
level_5: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations

level_1: Recognizes the importance of personal and professional well- being
level_2: Independently recognizes status of personal and professional well-being
level_3: With assistance, proposes a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_4: Independently develops a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_5: Participates in a system change to improve well- being in self and others

level_1: Demonstrates respect and establishes rapport in patient encounters

level_3: Identifies the need to adjust communication strategies to achieve shared decision making
Attempts to minimize communication barriers, including reflection on any biases
Mentors others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection to consistently develop positive therapeutic relationships
level_4: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in routine patient encounters
With guidance, uses shared decision making to implement a personalized care plan

level_5: Identifies barriers to effective communication in patient encounters

level_1: Respectfully receives a consultation request
With indirect supervision, completes consultations with effective documentation and communication in common cases
Facilitates team-based discussions to optimize team performance
level_2: Uses language that values all members of the health care team
Adapts communication style to fit team needs

level_3: With direct supervision, respectfully and thoroughly completes consultations with effective documentation and communication in common cases
Initiates team-based discussions to optimize team performance

level_4: Communicates information effectively with all health care team members
Completes consultations with effective documentation and communication in complex cases
level_5: Participates in team- based discussions to optimize team performance

level_1: Accurately records information in the patient record and safeguards patient personal health information

level_2: Demonstrates organized diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through notes in the patient record

level_3: Identifies appropriate communication channels (e.g., cell phone/pager usage, medical record, email) as required by institutional policy
